The 33rd China International Advertising Festival served as an important window for creative exchanges between Chinese and global advertising professionals. releases.body:
New capabilities link paid and organic AI performance across Bluefish agentic marketing suite.

NEW YORK, Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Bluefish, the Agentic Marketing Platform (AMP) for Fortune 500 brands, today announced its expansion into paid media. These new capabilities bring organic and paid AI marketing together across the platform's four core pillars: AI Monitoring, AI Optimization, AI Orchestration, and AI Measurement. The launch marks a significant evolution of the Bluefish AMP, extending its foundation in organic Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) to help enterprises move toward orchestrating every lever that shapes their brand's performance in AI.

The boundaries between organic visibility, paid advertising, and brand influence are converging, as AI reshapes consumer purchase decisions. In this emerging agentic funnel, effective advertising depends on understanding the context in which ads appear in AI, including which competitors are recommended and how products are positioned. Marketers need decision-grade intelligence to understand where paid investment can have the greatest impact for their target audiences.

The Bluefish AMP identifies where a brand is absent, misrepresented, or already recommended in AI-generated answers, directs paid media to those gaps and opportunities, and measures the overall impact. With Paid Media Briefs, available today as an extension of the Bluefish Optimization Suite, media teams receive platform-specific ad targeting, creative, and landing page recommendations designed to improve paid media performance across Google and ChatGPT.

The need for a unified approach is accelerating as AI advertising grows. U.S. spending on advertising adjacent to AI-powered search results is projected to reach $26.4 billion in 2026, according to EMARKETER, while ChatGPT Ads has reached approximately $1 billion in annualized revenue run rate.

Still, most paid media teams lack visibility into the organic AI context surrounding their paid placements. New Bluefish Intelligence research found across 5,810 buying topics and 3 categories, different brands lead AI-generated answers on Google and ChatGPT in 35% of cases. Advertising that is relevant on one AI platform may be poorly aligned with the answers consumers receive on another. These variations make organic AI intelligence critical to understanding where paid investment can have the greatest impact.

"The agentic funnel doesn't distinguish between organic and paid marketing, and neither should the platforms marketers use to manage it," said Alex Sherman, cofounder and CEO of Bluefish. "For decades, marketers have organized around channels, with separate teams, tools, and strategies for organic and paid media. But AI is collapsing those boundaries. We're expanding Bluefish to give enterprise marketers a unified way to orchestrate that experience end-to-end."

The Future of Agentic Ads

Beginning with coverage of Google and ChatGPT, Bluefish's AMP is expanding to support additional paid media levers, including sponsored publisher content, creator partnerships, user-generated content, and retail media. Through MCP and API integrations, Bluefish is also developing capabilities to bring this intelligence into existing enterprise marketing workflows.

The result is a new operating model for agentic marketing: one that connects paid and organic strategies, coordinates execution across marketing functions, and creates a more complete picture of brand performance in AI.

"AI is fundamentally changing how marketing strategies are built and executed," said Jing Feng, cofounder and COO at Bluefish. "A brand's AI signal is becoming a critical input into marketing decisions, from where to invest to which campaigns to prioritize and how to measure their impact. We're building Bluefish to make that intelligence the foundation for orchestrating enterprise marketing across every team."

About Bluefish

Bluefish is the Agentic Marketing Platform (AMP) for the Fortune 500. The platform helps the world's largest brands orchestrate their AI performance across major platforms like ChatGPT and Google Gemini. Brands including Adidas, American Express, eBay, Hearst, Tishman Speyer and others use Bluefish to ensure their products and services are accurately portrayed in AI-generated responses consumers see every day. Since launching in 2024, Bluefish has scaled to over 10% of the Fortune 500, with hundreds of enterprise accounts spanning 15 verticals including travel, financial services, CPG, luxury and beauty. To learn more, please visit www.bluefishai.com.

Competitive Renewal Launches New Era of Digital, Experiential and Branded Media as ECP Undergoes Major Terminal Expansion

PANAMA CITY, Fla., Oct. 27, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Clear Channel Outdoor (CCO)'s Airports Division, the leading U.S. airport sponsorship and advertising partner, has renewed and expanded its longstanding partnership with Northwest Florida Beaches International Airport (ECP). Originally established in 2005 and reselected through a competitive process, the renewed agreement reflects two decades of operational performance and the airport's confidence in CCO's ability to deliver on its next chapter of growth.

The agreement comes as ECP undertakes a major terminal expansion and modernization project, creating an opportunity for CCO to invest more into the airport's advertising program with new digital media, experiential activations and refreshed displays. The centerpiece of the new program will be a network of double-sided digital flags throughout the concourse, introducing dynamic content and a contemporary digital media presence that integrates seamlessly and enhances the terminal environment.

Under the new agreement, CCO will make a significant investment in ECP's advertising infrastructure over an initial three-year contract term and with the opportunity to renew. The investment will support the evolution of a curated and contemporary advertising program, with strategically positioned state-of-the-art media that complements the passenger experience and the airport's sense of place. The program will provide greater flexibility for advertisers while creating new opportunities for brands to engage travelers and support ECP's long-term commercial growth.

"ECP is a market that performs well above its size, and this renewal is a reflection of what a strong collaborative partnership produces over time," said Morten Gotterup, president, Clear Channel Outdoor's Airports Division. "As ECP invests in the next generation of its terminal, we have an opportunity to invest into that experience and to build something that reflects both where this airport is today and where it's headed. Our new program will bring together digital, experiential and high-impact media to continue to delight passengers and the brands that want to reach them for years to come."

ECP has experienced sustained growth since opening in 2010, serving a record 1.9 million passengers in 2025 representing a 3.1% year-over-year increase. The airport serves large, leisure-oriented audiences, with travelers visiting Northwest Florida's Emerald Coast for vacations, weekend getaways and outdoor recreation. Through nonstop and seasonal service from American, Delta, Southwest and United Airlines, ECP connects the region with major markets including Atlanta, Nashville, Dallas, Denver, Houston, New York, Chicago and Baltimore. That traveler profile—arriving and ready to engage—makes ECP a compelling platform for brands looking to connect with consumers at the start of their trip.

"As ECP undergoes this major Terminal Expansion, we are focused on enhancing every element of the traveler experience. Clear Channel's commitment to investing in state-of-the-art digital infrastructure and experiential activations will not only modernize our concourses but also provide powerful new avenues for local and national brands to connect with our growing passenger base. We are proud to build upon our history together and look forward to a new era of innovation that supports ECP's long-term commercial vitality," stated ECP Executive Director Parker W. McClellan Jr., A.A.E.

The renewed partnership reflects CCO and ECP's shared commitment to evolving the airport experience alongside the continued growth of Northwest Florida. As construction progresses toward the terminal expansion's 2029 completion, the new advertising program will provide a flexible platform that grows with the airport creating new opportunities for brands to connect with travelers while supporting ECP's long-term revenue goals.

To learn more about Clear Channel Airports, visit https://clearchanneloutdoor.com/airport-advertising/.

Clear Channel Outdoor Holdings, Inc. is at the forefront of driving innovation in the out-of-home advertising industry. Our dynamic advertising platform is broadening the pool of advertisers using its medium through the expansion of digital billboards and displays and the integration of data analytics and programmatic capabilities that deliver measurable campaigns that are simpler to buy. By leveraging the scale, reach and flexibility of our diverse portfolio of assets, we connect advertisers with millions of consumers every month.

releases.title: Cuttable Unveils Next-Generation AI Advertising Platform as U.S. Expansion Accelerates
releases.body:
The platform's evolution comes alongside an A$20 million Series A funding round led by Airtree Ventures, marking Cuttable's next phase of growth as it moves beyond AI ad generation.

NEW YORK, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cuttable, an AI-powered creative production platform for performance marketing teams, today unveiled the next evolution of its platform, designed to help brands move beyond generating ads to understand what works and make smarter decisions about what to create next. Just one year after entering the U.S. market, the Australian-founded company now generates 40% of its revenue from the region.

While AI has made producing ads faster and easier, knowing which creative to make next remains a challenge. Most tools focus on either generating ads or analyzing their performance, leaving marketers to connect the dots between what they intend to test, what actually worked and what to create next.

Cuttable brings those pieces together. Its evolved platform connects a brand's creative assets, customer data and performance history with the marketer's original intent, building on what the brand has already tried rather than starting from scratch with each new creative brief.

Cuttable's software was built to remove creative as a bottleneck for performance marketing teams producing, testing and rebuilding ads at scale. The platform reads a brand's website, social channels and guidelines to build an editable brand strategy and brand kit. From there, marketers can write a brief in plain language and receive finished, editable ads, built using existing brand and product assets or Cuttable's AI content studio, Shoots, which creates and extends photo and video content.

Finished ads publish directly to Meta Ads Manager, and Cuttable's Ad Insights reads the performance back from Meta, including thumbstop, click-through rate and return on ad spend, so that the next brief builds on what worked. It's this continuous feedback loop, rather than creative generation alone, that differentiates Cuttable from tools that separately generate ads or report on performance. 

Cuttable's Co-founder & CEO, Sam Kroonenburg, who previously founded and sold A Cloud Guru in 2021, said, "Creative is still made the way it was thirty years ago, one ad at a time. Making an ad has never been the hard part, it is knowing which one to make next. We are building the creative production system ecommerce performance marketers have been waiting for."

Across 280,000 ads and more than $320 million in Meta spend run through its platform, Cuttable found that one ad in eleven returns ten times its spend or better, and that a small number of ads end up carrying an entire account. The company's data also shows brands increase creative output 3.4 times going into November, underscoring the growing pressure to produce and test ads at scale.

In just two years since launching, Cuttable now works with more than 420 brands across the United States, Australia, New Zealand, Asia and Europe, including lululemon, Rodan & Fields and Brick. Brands on the platform average a 4.4 times return on ad spend and see a 37 percent lift in account-level return on ad spend after moving to Cuttable. To support its growing U.S. business, Cuttable is actively hiring and building out its San Francisco team.

Airtree, which first invested in Cuttable earlier this year, returned to lead the round. One of Australia's largest technology investors, its portfolio includes Canva, Airwallex, Linktree and SafetyCulture.

Airtree Ventures partner James Cameron, whose firm also backed A Cloud Guru, said: "Since we backed Cuttable's seed round, their growth has been much faster than our (already very high) expectations. The world of ad creative is being turned on its head by AI, and we're excited to lead this round as Cuttable becomes the leading system that performance marketers reach for to make content work harder."

With the U.S. already emerging as a major growth market, Cuttable plans to use its latest funding to accelerate its expansion and advance the next evolution of its platform. Cuttable's focus from here is on closing the creative loop, helping marketers decide what to make next rather than only how to make it.

ABOUT CUTTABLE

Cuttable is a creative production platform for performance marketing teams, used by more than 420 brands across the United States, Australia, New Zealand, Asia and Europe. The company is headquartered in New York with offices in Melbourne and San Francisco.

To learn more, visit cuttable.com.

The complete, corrected release follows:

IAB Opens Public Comment on New Guide to Inform Cross-Channel Measurement Decisions

New "Project Eidos" Output Gives Marketers a Decision-First Approach to Interpreting and Applying MMM, Incrementality, and Attribution Results

Public Comment Open Through November 4, 2026

NEW YORK, Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB), the leading trade organization for the digital advertising ecosystem, today announced the release of its Cross-Channel Measurement Decision Guide for public comment. Developed as part of Project Eidos, the guide advances IAB's work to help marketers use cross-channel measurement evidence to make better-informed investment and optimization decisions. Public comment is open through November 4, 2026.

The guide gives marketers, agency teams, and measurement partners a decision-first approach to selecting, interpreting, and applying evidence from methods like Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM), incrementality testing, and attribution, including when their findings appear to tell conflicting stories. Rather than starting with whatever metrics happen to be available, it starts with the business decision at hand and works backward to the evidence best suited to inform it.

"Measurement only works if the industry has confidence in the answers it produces, and right now, MMM, incrementality, and attribution can each tell a different story about the same campaign," said David Cohen, CEO, IAB. "This guide doesn't ask marketers to pick a winner among those methods. It gives them a disciplined way to work through the options and make an informed decision they can trust. That's exactly the kind of foundational work Project Eidos was built to do."

The guide has three connected parts:

  • The Decision Guide: Lays out a decision-first sequence, from business outcome to decision, measurement question, measurement approach, evidence, interpretation, and action
  • The Decision Navigator: Applies that sequence to common decisions, such as allocating budget across channels or assessing whether an investment is creating incremental value, and helps readers determine which methods fit the question and how to weigh the evidence
  • The Measurement Reference Library: Brings together existing metric definitions and supporting context to help readers interpret the evidence used in the Decision Guide and Decision Navigator

"We built this to be used, not just read," said Matt Shapo, Senior Director, Measurement, IAB. "The real test is whether it holds up in an actual planning conversation, like when a channel reports a strong attributed ROAS that an incrementality test doesn't back up. That's exactly the kind of scenario we want the industry weighing in on before we finalize it."

IAB is especially seeking feedback on whether the guide reflects real-world measurement decisions, whether its method-fit and interpretation guidance holds up when results conflict, and whether its scenarios are realistic enough for day-to-day planning. The release directly supports IAB's mission to drive growth, trust, and innovation across the digital advertising ecosystem.

"Marketers rely on measurement to make consequential investment decisions, but they don't always feel confident that their approaches deliver the evidence they need," said David Cohen, CEO, IAB. "60–75% of marketers say advanced measurement falls short across key dimensions such as rigor, timeliness, trust, and efficiency, and this guide helps them connect evidence from different measurement approaches to the decision at hand. It also helps them understand what the findings can support, and identify where additional testing or calibration is needed. That gives brands and their partners a stronger foundation for putting measurement into action."

The public comment period is open from October 20, 2026 through November 4, 2026. To review the Cross-Channel Measurement Decision Guide and submit feedback, click https://www.iab.com/guidelines/cross-channel-measurement-guide-open-for-15-day-public-comment/

About IAB

The Interactive Advertising Bureau (IAB) empowers the media and marketing industries to thrive in the digital economy. Its membership comprises more than 700 leading media companies, brands, agencies, and the technology firms responsible for selling, delivering, and optimizing digital ad marketing campaigns. The trade group fields critical research on interactive advertising, while also educating brands, agencies, and the wider business community on the importance of digital marketing. In affiliation with the IAB Tech Lab, IAB develops technical standards and solutions. IAB is committed to professional development and elevating the knowledge, skills, expertise, and collaboration of the workforce across the industry. Through the work of its public policy office in Washington, D.C., the trade association advocates for its members and promotes the value of the interactive advertising industry to legislators and policymakers. Founded in 1996, IAB is headquartered in New York City.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Oct. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- OnVibe, an AI-powered social marketing company backed by LG NOVA, LG Electronics' North America Innovation Center, today unveiled a new agentic AI system that powers its social marketing platform, carrying business context from content recommendations through creation and Instagram publishing.

AI has made it easy to generate a post in seconds. As feeds fill with content that looks and sounds alike, the harder work is knowing which ideas reflect a business, connect with its audience and deserve a place in the feed. For founders and small teams, that work competes with building products, serving customers and running day-to-day operations.

The system brings together ideas, writing, visual creation, scheduling and Instagram publishing in one conversation, helping businesses turn ideas into finished posts with fewer steps. It delivers daily content ideas shaped by each business's context and helps users develop their chosen ideas into finished posts. Users can also ask it to develop a content plan and schedule posts across multiple days.

"Small teams have enough to do without figuring out what to ask an AI each morning," said OnVibe CEO Sahar Arshad. "OnVibe looks at what has worked for your business, what your audience responds to and what is happening in your niche. It brings you ideas with a reason behind each one. You choose the direction, and the same conversation can take it all the way to publication."

Acting as a personal AI agent for the business's Instagram, OnVibe has an informed memory and adapts to the client's work style to provide professional, customized guidance aligned with the business's needs and goals, so businesses can confidently decide what to post.

OnVibe's VibeCheck helps businesses and creators understand what's working in their social content, where the gaps are and what to post next. It evaluates positioning, content pillars and engagement patterns, then provides suggested posts and practical recommendations to strengthen their social presence. For accounts with existing content, OnVibe can analyze up to 50 recent posts to understand content patterns and audience response. The feature helps users assess posting consistency, engagement and content formats.

Free evaluations are available at audit.onvibe.co, with no platform signup required, for Instagram business and creator accounts, as well as LinkedIn profiles of founders and executives and LinkedIn company pages.

How the New System Works

OnVibe's agentic system is designed to carry context and work across the steps involved in social marketing:

  • Ideas that arrive ready to develop: Daily Drop offers content ideas tailored to the business, with creative direction, suggested copy or scripts, captions, hashtags and visuals. Each idea includes an explanation of why it was recommended.
  • Memory users can shape: OnVibe builds on what it learns about a business's voice, visual style, goals, location, market and preferences across conversations. Users can review and update that memory, upload their own images and add PDF brand guidelines. They can also ask why a particular idea fits.
  • A conversation that adapts to the task: Users can request a precise edit or provide a broader brief. They can refine a static post, build a carousel or generate a multi-day content plan, then schedule or publish finished posts directly to Instagram within the same conversation.
  • Writing guided by practitioners: Captions follow guidance developed by OnVibe's social media experts to help the writing sound specific to the business.

The free Starter Plan supports one connected Instagram account and requires no credit card. Higher creation limits are currently available at no cost for a limited time.

Expert Support Through OnVibe Concierge

OnVibe's Concierge program provides businesses with a team to manage their social presence using OnVibe's Agentic AI Engine. Its strategists and creatives handle social strategy, content creation, publishing and performance across Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok and Facebook, using OnVibe's AI engine as the backend to refine the work over time. In two months, OnVibe Concierge helped an early-stage technology client triple its follower count while increasing posting frequency from one to five posts per week across four social channels. To build awareness and make the product's value more relatable, OnVibe developed a consistent brand voice, content built around real-world experiences, user-generated content and a paid distribution strategy.

Concierge supports ongoing social marketing as well as company launches, product introductions and entry into new markets, including international businesses launching in the U.S. The team helps sharpen the message and carry the story across the channels where the business needs to build an audience.

The event was held live at Morphy's Pennsylvania gallery, with all forms of remote bidding available. Morphy's has long-been renowned as the auction house collectors depend on for rare automobilia and petroliana.

The 1932 Cadillac 355-B seven-passenger Imperial limousine with body by Fisher was finished in cream with burgundy fenders and accents. A binder documented nearly $95,000 worth of mechanical restoration, refurbishment and detailing had been performed by Classic & Exotic Service in 2011 and 2012. A New York Certificate of Sale identified notorious Prohibition-era gangster Alphonse "Al" Capone as its original purchaser/owner. Rochelle Cadillac Co., of New Rochelle, New York, was shown as the seller.

The well-documented 1964 Chevrolet Impala finished in silver blue metallic over a coordinated blue bucket-seat interior had a VIN # of 41447S178226, identifying it as a genuine St Louis-built V-8 Super Sport hardtop. Power was supplied by Chevy's dual-quad 409-c.i. engine, producing 425 horsepower thru 11.0:1 compression. The odometer displayed 52,659 miles. The car started with ease and the drive was very smooth.

Following the two automobiles, the auction's number three top achiever was a1906 Indian Camelback motorized bicycle built by The Hendree Manufacturing Company (later The Indian Motocycle Company, with no "R" in motorcycle). The bike was a true survivor in barn-fresh condition, retaining its factory paint job in Springfield Blue, while the 311 cubic inch, 2.25-hp air-cooled single-cylinder motor with a production number of 2877 was untouched, with all major components intact. The motor turned over with good compression, the wheels spun freely, and the brakes worked just fine. One lucky bidder "rode" it home for $61,500.

A Gilbarco gas pump originally found in Northern California, one of very few known examples with a porcelain Mohawk Indian computing face, changed hands for $31,980, topping the $30,000 high estimate. The pump's condition was described as being like NOS (new/old stock). The color and gloss were perfect, with no notable wear to the Indian graphic, and it lit up nicely.

There were two bona fide "sleepers" in the sale. One was a circa-1930s single-sided porcelain flange sign graded 9.0 for the Pickwick Stages Ticket Office, an excellent example of a seldom-seen sign. Each side displayed excellent color and gloss, with no noticeable field wear. The 28¾-inch by 25½-inch sign more than doubled the $8,000 high estimate, reaching $19,680.

The second of the two sleepers was just as impressive. It was a circa-1930s Zeroline ("The Standard Oil For Motor Cars") single-sided porcelain sign, 23¾ inches in diameter and graded 9.0 out of 10 for condition. The sign showed very good color throughout and a great graphic, which no doubt helped it to more than double its $12,000 high estimate and realize a robust $28,800.

releases.body:
Reshift Media's flagship quarterly franchise development report reveals a 40.7% decline in ownership search demand from early-2026 highs, while advertising engagement rises 26.8%, inquiry conversion increases 166.6%, and lead generation costs fall 68%.

NEW YORK, Oct. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Franchise ownership interest in the United States is returning to historic levels following an exceptional surge earlier this year, and new research suggests prospective franchisees are becoming significantly more responsive to recruitment advertising. According to The Franchise Development Outlook: Q3 2026, the flagship quarterly franchise development intelligence report from Reshift Media and Franify, active franchise ownership search demand has declined considerably from its February peak while advertising engagement and inquiry conversion rates have strengthened dramatically.

The full Q3 2026 Franchise Development Outlook report, available as a free download, includes proprietary franchise development indices, historical trends, advertising performance data, economic analysis, and forecasts through March 2027.

The report's proprietary Franchise Development Demand Index (FDDI), which tracks U.S. Google search interest related to franchise ownership, reached 107.6 in September 2026, down 40.7% from its February peak of 181.4. Despite the decline, search demand remains 7.6% above its 2022–2024 historical baseline. Reshift Media forecasts a continued return toward normal levels through the remainder of 2026, followed by a modest seasonal recovery in early 2027.

However, the report reveals a contrasting trend in franchise recruitment advertising. Engagement with outbound social media franchise advertisements increased 26.8% compared with Q3 2025, while the rate at which advertising clicks generated franchise inquiries increased 166.6%. At the same time, the indexed cost per inquiry declined 68.0% year-over-year.

"The most interesting finding is the growing disconnect between active franchise ownership searches and advertising engagement," said Steve Buors, CEO and Co-Founder of Reshift Media. "We're seeing fewer people actively searching for franchise opportunities than we did earlier this year, but the people responding to franchise advertising are engaging at much higher rates. For franchisors, that suggests there is still considerable opportunity to generate interest and inquiries with the right advertising strategy, even as overall search demand returns to more typical levels."

Franchise Ownership Demand Expected to Normalize Through Early 2027

The FDDI measures relative search interest across a basket of franchise ownership-related terms, indexed to a 2022–2024 baseline of 100. During Q3 2026, the index averaged 111.9, representing a 15.2% decline compared with the same quarter in 2025.

Although active search demand remains above historical norms, the report forecasts continued moderation through Q4 2026, with the FDDI projected to average 102.8. A modest seasonal rebound is expected in Q1 2027, when the index is forecast to average 111.0, considerably below the exceptional levels recorded in early 2026.

The research also identifies elevated financing costs, persistent inflation, weak consumer confidence, and broader economic uncertainty as factors that may continue to influence prospective franchisees' investment decisions.

Advertising Performance Points to a More Responsive Audience

While the volume of active franchise ownership searches has declined, Reshift Media's proprietary advertising indices suggest that people encountering franchise opportunities through outbound advertising are increasingly willing to engage.

The Franchise Advertising Engagement Index reached 117.4 in Q3 2026, its strongest third-quarter reading in the available dataset. The Franchise Advertising Inquiry Conversion Index climbed to 229.5, indicating that a substantially higher proportion of advertising clicks are generating recorded franchise inquiries compared with a year earlier.

These improvements have contributed to a sharp reduction in inquiry generation costs. The Franchise Advertising Cost Per Inquiry Index reached 40.2 in September 2026, down from 125.8 in Q3 2025.

The findings suggest that although fewer individuals may be proactively researching franchise ownership, there remains strong interest among prospective candidates who encounter relevant opportunities through advertising.

"For franchise development teams, this reinforces the importance of reaching beyond people who are already searching for a franchise," added Buors. "Search marketing remains essential, but effective outbound advertising can introduce franchise opportunities to people who may be interested in business ownership without actively looking for it. The data suggests those audiences are responding particularly well right now."

The report cautions that higher advertising engagement and inquiry conversion do not necessarily translate directly into qualified franchise candidates or completed franchise sales.

AI Is Emerging as Another Franchise Discovery Channel

Beyond advertising performance, the report examines the growing influence of artificial intelligence on franchise candidate research.

Research cited in the report indicates that ChatGPT usage among U.S. adults has increased substantially, reaching 44% in 2026. Additionally, a September 2026 study found that 27% of surveyed franchise prospects identified ChatGPT as one of their most useful tools when researching franchise opportunities.

These findings highlight the growing importance of ensuring franchise information is accessible, accurate, and discoverable across AI-powered research platforms, alongside traditional search engines, franchise directories, and digital advertising channels.

About The Franchise Development Outlook

The Franchise Development Outlook is Reshift Media and Franify's flagship quarterly franchise development intelligence report, providing original research into U.S. franchise ownership demand, recruitment advertising performance, economic conditions, and emerging candidate research behaviors.

The Q3 2026 edition includes four proprietary franchise development indices, historical trend analysis, advertising engagement and inquiry conversion data, economic indicators, and forecasts through March 2027.

The complete Franchise Development Outlook: Q3 2026 report is available to download free of charge.

Reshift Media is an award-winning digital marketing agency specializing in franchise and multi-location organizations. Serving more than 200 clients across 22 countries, Reshift Media provides digital marketing strategy, paid media, search engine optimization, social media marketing, website development, and proprietary marketing technology designed for the unique needs of franchise organizations.

Franify is Reshift Media's proprietary franchise digital marketing platform, designed to help franchisors and franchisees coordinate, execute, and optimize digital marketing campaigns across multiple locations.

Audience Insights brings key campaign intelligence into a simplified view, helping advertisers move beyond standard campaign delivery metrics to better understand the audiences they are reaching. Through Audience Insights, advertisers can uncover content and media consumption patterns across their campaigns, including the shows, programming, and entertainment their audiences engage with, the publishers and channels delivering that content, and the markets and ZIP codes where those audiences live.

That visibility is possible because of fullthrottle.ai's direct relationships with premium publishers, including Nexstar, iHeartMedia, TuneIn, Roku, Spectrum, SiriusXM (Pandora), Comcast Advertising, and TelevisaUnivision, combined with Immersive Household® delivery that connects a single household's behavior across CTV, audio, display, video, and direct mail. Audience Insights also reflects activations available within the fullthrottle.ai® platform across additional premium publishers, including Warner Bros. Discovery, FOX, Spotify, Hearst, and AMP Media.

Most comparable reports in the category answer a narrower question: where the ads ran. That is a defensive screen, built to confirm delivery after the fact. Because Audience Insights is built on first-party data and SafeMatch® attribution, it answers a different question: where real shoppers and actual transacting customers are consuming media. Advertisers can see the placements, the channels, and the show-level content and domain-level destinations where their buyers spend time. fullthrottle.ai® believes the best defense is a good offense. These insights extend beyond a single campaign, giving advertisers a real psychographic view of real buyers that can inform media planning and buying across traditional and digital channels alike.

For multi-market advertisers, campaign-level reporting can also reveal differences between individual markets. Campaigns targeting different geographies can surface distinct publisher and media consumption patterns, giving advertisers a more localized view of audience behavior.

When advertisers set up individual markets as separate campaigns, each campaign has its own Audience Insights reporting. This allows advertisers to see market-specific differences, including local publishers and media consumption patterns, without combining the reporting across markets.

The campaign also won Gold in Food & Beverage and Silver for Best Brand Transformation. The Grand Ogilvy recognizes the year's most compelling connection between research, consumer insight, creative work and results.

The Fairlife and Doner team used post-workout interviews, in-home discussions, semiotic analysis, barrier research, brand tracking and creative testing to understand how people approach exercise and recovery. "Champion Your Recovery" turned that insight into a more inclusive invitation to recognize effort at every level.

The winners were celebrated October 14 at Tribeca Rooftop in New York City, following the ARF's Creative Effectiveness conference. Nicely Network reports more than 15,000 AI citations generated, more than $150 million in tracked sales revenue, more than 300 brands served, including Fortune 500 companies, and more than 160 million views across ranked discussions.

The agency combines Reddit Marketing with Article Placements. The objective is to create content that can perform in multiple discovery environments rather than relying on a single channel.

"Reddit has become part of the research process behind both search results and AI answers," the Expert Consumers editorial team said. "The value of a campaign increasingly depends on whether useful discussions remain discoverable and continue contributing to visibility after publication."

The Role of Reddit in AI Visibility

Reddit is a central part of Nicely Network's strategy because the platform already carries significant visibility across product research and AI search.

The media kit cites data showing Reddit as the most prominent site across 10,000 "best [product]" Google searches. Separate 2026 Semrush data cited in the media kit shows Reddit appearing in 11.29% of ChatGPT Search, Perplexity and Google AI Mode responses, ahead of LinkedIn, Wikipedia and YouTube.

For brands, this creates a link between Reddit marketing and Generative Engine Optimisation. Discussions can rank in Google, remain visible on Reddit and become sources that AI systems can retrieve when users ask recommendation-oriented questions.

Reddit discussions are also structured around the language buyers actually use. Nicely Network builds discussions around high-intent keywords and places them in communities where consumers already ask for recommendations. Supporting comments reinforce the recommendation while replies and engagement help discussions remain visible.

Results Across Reddit and AI Search

The Best Reddit Marketing Agency recognition for October 2026 also reflects results shown across Nicely Network's case studies.

In the outdoor category, one campaign reached 60,000 AI mentions per month, up from near zero, while AI impressions reached 48 million per month across seven AI platforms.

In cybersecurity, 10 discussions generated more than 250 citations for an antivirus brand, while its ChatGPT share of voice increased from 6% to 17%.

A health and wellness campaign reached the number one position for AI visibility in its category. The media kit reports a 200% increase in AI mentions over four months.

In the DTC furniture category, a Reddit campaign generated $150,000 in tracked sales, 21,190 clicks to the company website and 1 million organic discussion views. The campaign also recorded 35x more AI Overview mentions and 210x more ChatGPT mentions.

Another privacy software campaign reached 158,000 views, with more than 10,000 additional views per month coming from search and AI citations. The discussion was shown as a source in both Google AI Overview and ChatGPT.

AI-SEO Article Placements Add a Second Discovery Layer

Nicely Network also uses high-authority article placements to support AI visibility and search performance. The agency develops AI-SEO optimized articles designed to provide clear, structured information that can be retrieved by search engines and language models.

Results presented in the media kit include a health and longevity article that generated 16,924 views, 2,483 clicks and 14,730 Google and AI retrievals. An education article recorded 18,379 views and a 35% click-through rate, with 15,593 Google and AI retrievals.

Software content recorded 13,522 views, a 31% click-through rate and 11,363 Google and AI retrievals. A health supplement article generated 13,417 views, a 25% click-through rate and 10,957 Google and AI retrievals.

These placements give the agency's AI-SEO strategy another source type beyond Reddit. Together, Reddit discussions and editorial articles can provide material that appears across conventional search and AI-driven discovery.

A Measurement Model Built Around AI Visibility

Nicely Network measures campaigns across three areas: AI search visibility, SEO and organic visibility, and content performance.

AI search visibility covers mentions, citations, impressions and share of voice across leading LLMs. SEO and organic visibility tracks discussions and articles appearing for targeted Google searches. Content performance measures views, engagement, click-throughs and sales tracked through affiliate links or UTM parameters.

The agency's reporting examples also show how campaign content can become a direct source for AI systems. In one ChatGPT example, three of the five cited sources were campaign discussions.

The model reflects a broader change in how digital visibility is evaluated. A ranking position is no longer the only useful outcome when consumers increasingly use ChatGPT, Google AI Overview, Google Gemini and Perplexity to compare products, services and recommendations.

Engagement Plans for Brands

Nicely Network offers engagement levels based on campaign scale and duration.

The Starter plan is priced at $5,000 to $15,000 per month for one to three months and includes five to 15 Reddit discussions and two to five AI-SEO articles.

Leadership engagements range from $30,000 to $60,000 per month and include 40 to 80 Reddit discussions and 10 to 30 AI-SEO articles. Enterprise engagements are also available for multi-brand portfolios and larger programs covering multiple product categories or markets.

The agency recommends longer engagements for brands pursuing sustained AI-SEO visibility, allowing content deployment and visibility gains to build over time.

Who the Approach Suits

The model is designed for brands whose customers research options through recommendations, comparisons and category-specific questions. That includes software and B2B companies, technology brands, retail and consumer products, fashion and beauty, nutrition and wellness, finance, and travel.

For these categories, the relevant opportunity is not simply generating more content. It is creating discussions and articles that answer the questions buyers are already asking, then measuring whether those assets become visible in search and AI answers.

releases.title: OMNICOM MEDIA AND REMBRAND PARTNER TO SCALE IN-CONTENT ADVERTISING ACROSS PREMIUM STREAMING
releases.body:
First-to-market capability brings together Acxiom, Omni, and Rembrand's VISTA platform, with access to premium inventory from major media partners

NEW YORK, Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Omnicom Media, an Omnicom (NYSE: OMC) Connected Capability, and in-content advertising platform Rembrand are partnering to bring in-content advertising into the mainstream media mix with a first-to-market capability that enables brands to identify, plan, and activate in-content placements across first-look premium streaming inventory from multiple major media companies.

The partnership provides OM's Content Collective – the group's branded content center of excellence - first-mover access to Rembrand's AI-powered VISTA platform, which scans publisher content to identify scenes that can be monetized by insertion of in-content advertising. Using AcxiomRealID™ and direct integrations with major streamers, brands can identify the most relevant content for a given audience. Pairing this intelligence with Rembrand's VISTA platform, brands unlock a more systematic and scalable way to find relevant programming and activate against those opportunities across participating streaming partners.

Historically, in-content advertising has been managed through bespoke partnerships and individual content integrations. The new capability brings those opportunities into a common planning framework, giving media teams visibility across participating publishers and allowing in-content placements to be considered alongside broader media investments.

The collaboration is rooted in a fundamental shift in consumer behavior. Omnicom Media's recent research, From Tuned Out to Leaned In: How to Combat Ad Avoidance, found that 65% of U.S. consumers avoid advertising to some degree, whether by skipping, scrolling, muting, or ignoring ads. As consumers use subscriptions, apps, AI, and other tools to exert greater control over their media experiences, brands need new ways to reach people without creating another interruption.

Additionally, commissioned research conducted by Omnicom Media's Partner Intelligence team in collaboration with Rembrand evaluated the effectiveness of in-content advertising, finding that, when paired with traditional video ads, perceptions of premium content amplify the performance of ICAs, driving a 5.5 times impact on message recall, and a 4x increase in both purchase intent and perceptions of the brand as premium.

"Our research identified how quickly consumers actively or passively disengage when advertising feels intrusive or overly repetitive," said Megan Pagliuca, Chief Product Officer, Omnicom Media. "To address this, we have launched new capabilities in streaming to address negative reach, improve relevance and measurability of traditional brand experiences, and now we are complementing these with a first of its kind data driven, scalable approach to in-content advertising."

How It Works

The capability connects four stages:

  • Audience matching: Acxiom audience segments are matched with streaming viewership data to identify shows, movies, and genres that best index with a target audience.
  • Inventory mapping: Relevant programming is matched against in-content advertising opportunities available through VISTA.
  • Inventory expansion: Additional content can be onboarded through established processes with participating streaming partners when relevant opportunities are not yet available.
  • Activation: Brands deploy in-content placements against selected audiences and programming across participating publishers.

The result is a way to put brands directly into content consumers have chosen to watch, while providing greater visibility into in-content supply across publishers.

"In-content advertising has always offered brands the opportunity to show up within content people have actively chosen to watch," said John Sedlak, Chief Revenue Officer, Rembrand. "Our collaboration with Omnicom Media makes those opportunities easier to identify, plan and activate across premium streaming, bringing a new level of scale and consistency to the category."

Applications range from an automaker placing a new model in relevant programming across a streamer, using Acxiom in-market auto segments to reach shoppers who routinely avoid traditional ads, to a beverage brand appearing in top-indexing summer programming during key seasonal purchase periods. Retail brands can similarly use in-content placements to directly connect exposure to the path to purchase.

Summing up the response to-date from clients who have been briefed on the new capability, Jillian Davis, Director of Marketing Technology for Auto Trader and Kelly Blue Book parent company Cox Automotive said, "We're always eager to leverage new, scalable and organic ways to reach our customers within premium content."

Longtime partners in independent ad-quality measurement add an AI agent that automatically recovers wasted Google Ads spend for brand advertisers, globally.

NEW YORK and MUNICH, Oct. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FouAnalytics, the independent analytics platform for digital ads, websites and mobile apps, today announced a deeper partnership with fraud0 to bring their world-first AI agent for automated ad refunds to the world's largest advertisers.

"Pharmaceutical company Uriach used fraud0 AI for Google Ads Refunds to recover $28,000 in Google Ads spend in just three months."

TULSA, Okla., Oct. 7, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- EMCO Industries, a leading manufacturer of leaf springs for trailers, agricultural equipment, recreational vehicles and specialty vehicles, announced that its new 30,000-square-foot automated manufacturing facility in Claremore, Oklahoma, is online and in production. The plant is dedicated exclusively to the heavy-duty trailer market. The company also announced the appointment of Wayne Sornberger as director of business development.

The facility represents a multimillion-dollar investment in automation and more than doubles EMCO's production capacity. Twelve robots work in tandem across the line, taking raw bars of American steel through shearing, tapering, forming, heat treating and quenching. The plant is expected to support approximately 20 new jobs in Claremore and the surrounding area.

Roughly a dozen heavy-duty spring configurations are now being produced on the automated line, including the High-Performance Mono-Leaf Spring EMCO introduced in January. That 22,400-pound gross-axle-weight-rated spring reduced component weight 25 percent, from 53 pounds to 40 pounds, and exceeds Truck Trailer Manufacturers Association B-10 fatigue life requirements.

"Bringing this plant online and appointing Wayne to lead our HD sales efforts are two key components of our strategy," said Marcus Hester, president of EMCO Industries. "We built capacity specifically for heavy-duty trailer springs, and we brought in someone who has spent his career in that segment and knows what those buyers need. The plant gives us the room to grow. Wayne gives us the relationships to fill it."

Sornberger joined EMCO on July 13 after 35 years in the spring industry. He will cover the heavy-duty trailer market across North America and works from Alberta, Canada. Over three decades he has served many of North America's largest and most demanding trailer manufacturers.

"Customers stay with people who solve their problems, and that starts with getting product on the dock when you say you will," Sornberger said. "What EMCO gives me to sell is a spring built in Oklahoma from American steel, an eight-week lead time instead of 16 or 20, and a supply line that isn't exposed to import tariffs. Those are the three things buyers ask me about first."

EMCO's domestic manufacturing footprint has become a competitive advantage as trailer manufacturers work to reduce exposure to offshore supply. Because the company produces its springs in Oklahoma using domestic steel, customers avoid the tariff costs and the shipping variability attached to imported components. Lead times average eight weeks from order to delivery.

The company has expanded its share of business with leading OEMs, in a market that moved toward dual sourcing and domestic supply following the pandemic-era shortages that left mid-sized manufacturers waiting behind larger accounts. EMCO's focus on leaf springs allows the company to commit production capacity and engineering attention to those customers.

"Quality and price are table stakes in this business. If you can't deliver, none of it matters," Hester said. "That is what has earned us the business we have won over the last several years, and it is what the new facility protects as volume grows. We are not asking customers to take that on faith. Our record is on their receiving docks."

Every EMCO heavy-duty spring is manufactured to the company's proprietary steel specification and heat-treating process, then individually dipped and painted for corrosion resistance. The company is ISO 9001:2015 certified and has received multiple OEM Supplier of the Year awards. Its engineering team brings more than 120 years of combined leaf spring experience.

EMCO is accepting orders for its full heavy-duty trailer spring line.

releases.body:
Buyer and seller agents transact directly on infrastructure built for agents, governed on both sides of every buy, with Compliant's media quality and governance signals in every decision

NEW YORK and LONDON , Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- pubX, which builds agent-to-agent infrastructure for advertising, today announced a $5 million Series A led by Chicago Ventures and the acquisition of Compliant, the media quality and governance company. Terms of the acquisition were not disclosed. Compliant will retain its name and operate as a pubX company, led by CEO Jamie Barnard. Within pubX, Jamie will take the role of President, Global Demand Growth, leading the company's global growth strategy across agencies, advertisers and the wider buy-side.

pubX builds the agents that plan, buy, sell and optimize advertising — and the infrastructure they transact on. Its buyer agents and seller agents work directly with one another, from brief to reporting, across every channel, so that more of every dollar reaches the media and the publisher behind it. pubX began on the publisher side, spending years helping publishers price and sell their inventory. Compliant, founded by former Unilever and P&G executives, has focused principally on the demand side, delivering measurable value to global brands and their agencies. The acquisition unites brand and publisher in one company, and that experience, on both sides of the market is what shaped the company's vision for something new: infrastructure designed from the ground up for agents to buy and sell directly. Built on the open Ad Context Protocol (AdCP), it works for buyer and seller alike.

Trust as the founding product principle

pubX was built on the premise that no one hands their media budget to a system they don't trust, so trust, transparency, and accountability are built into the infrastructure itself, on both sides of every transaction. Its agents are educated by pubX: governance checks on every buy, decisions that are reasoned, traced and auditable, with Compliant's quality signals shaping what they consider. The agents are guided by the client, on the brand's own brief, plan, publishers and commercial rules. People stay in control: the client sets the level of autonomy and approves the plan at key stages, and the agents execute inside those rules. As trust is earned, autonomy grows.

"Programmatic took this industry from fax machines and spreadsheets into more automated and real-time platforms in two short decades, and everything we've done since builds on that premise," said Andrew Mole, CEO and co-founder of pubX. "Agents let us finish what was started. You tell them how you buy, you sign off where it matters, and every page of the brief gets read every single time. For the first time, the infrastructure has caught up with what brands want to achieve with their advertising and how publishers want to sell."

"For years, brands have searched for high-quality, high-performing inventory with real, relevant and engaged audiences. Compliant built the Data Integrity and CTV Quality Indexes so that they could do that with certainty rather than speculation," said Jamie Barnard, CEO of Compliant. "Inside pubX, those media quality and governance signals sit in the decision itself, so an agent weighs them before it buys. This is what gives each CMO the confidence to trust pubX's agents."

"Every part of the advertising industry is asking how agents will improve buying and selling, and most answers so far are an agentic layer built on existing infrastructure. Co-founders Andrew Mole and Alex Rosen, pubX's CTO, have built advertising infrastructure before, and this time they built it for agents from the start, on both sides of the transaction, with a publisher base that already trusts them and a design that keeps the client in control. That is a rare starting position, and the Compliant acquisition makes it stronger," said Stuart Larkins, Co-founder & General Partner at Chicago Ventures.

The funding will support pubX's expansion in the United States, the build-out of its demand-side business serving brands and agencies, continued development of its buyer and seller agents on AdCP, and the integration of Compliant's signals across the platform.

"For a publisher, agentic buying is about discoverability. Buyer agents see the audiences and environments we actually have, backed by our first-party data, and that puts us in front of spend that never reached us before, in an environment we can win. It amplifies what our sales team already does well," said Stephanie Mazzamaro, Head of Revenue and Data, Paradium.AI, formerly The Arena Group.

"As advertising increasingly moves toward agentic buying, discoverability becomes critical," said Jason Taylor, Chief Revenue Officer, USA TODAY Co. "Publishers that invest in trusted content, engaged audiences, and brand-safe environments should be more visible to AI-powered buying platforms. The opportunity is to create a more transparent marketplace where quality is recognized and rewarded."

pubX at Advertising Week New York

On Wednesday, October 7, pubX will run a live agent-to-agent media buy at a private executive lunch during Advertising Week New York. A campaign for Reckitt's Mucinex brand will go from brief to live placement, with Reckitt's trading team approving the plan at key stages and publishers including Paradium.AI and USA TODAY Co. reviewing and accepting the campaign as it happens. Attendance is by invitation.

About pubX

pubX builds agent-to-agent infrastructure for advertising. Its buyer and seller agents, educated by pubX, trained by the client, and governed on both sides of every transaction, let brands, agencies and publishers plan, buy, sell and optimize media directly, with trust earned one campaign at a time. Learn more at www.pubx.ai

About Compliant

Compliant, a pubX company, is the media quality and governance company behind the Data Integrity and CTV Quality Indexes, used by leading global advertisers and industry bodies to measure data integrity and media quality across the supply chain. Learn more at www.compliant.global

About Chicago Ventures

Chicago Ventures is a seed-stage venture capital fund founded to fill a market gap in early-stage capital for tech companies outside traditional hubs like Silicon Valley, focusing on undercapitalized tech ecosystems in the Central U.S. and beyond. They lead seed rounds "before it's obvious" and operate a formal platform function that serves as a direct extension of portfolio companies' teams, with their network explicitly architected to provide customer introductions, expert help, and talent access at scale rather than just for sourcing deals. Learn more at www.chicagoventures.com

releases.body:

NEW YORK, Sept. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- GrowthLoop, a pioneer in agentic AI-powered marketing solutions, today released its 2026 Commerce Media Investment Index, revealing that activation speed and audience options have become decisive factors in where advertisers place retail and commerce media budgets. Conducted in partnership with Ascend2, the study surveyed nearly 300 U.S. and Canadian marketing professionals involved in retail media network (RMN) or commerce media network (CMN) advertising decisions.

The findings reveal what motivates advertisers to spend more with network partners and shed light on how execution friction could put that spend at risk:

  • 86% say slow audience fulfillment could cause them to reduce spend or leave a network partner, while 85% say they would pay a premium for same-day fulfillment.  
  • Nearly all respondents indicate that access to more segments would make them more likely to increase spend.
  • 32% of advertisers have reduced, paused, or reconsidered investment because of difficulty proving ROI to leadership.

"Advertisers are telling media networks how to win more budget: Provide better audiences, activate them faster, and deliver meaningful results quickly enough to inform the next campaign," said Anthony Rotio, co-founder and co-CEO of GrowthLoop. "As we've seen with customers like Gopuff, a warehouse-native audience building solution is the way to fulfill these requirements and ultimately build stronger advertiser relationships."

Key report findings

The Index shows that advertisers spread significant budget across a crowded commerce media market. The majority of advertisers allocate at least 15% of their digital advertising budgets to these networks and 90% work with two or more RMN or CMN partners. No respondents plan to decrease commerce media spend in the next year, and a full 85% plan to increase their spend.

Additional findings include:

Speed shapes spending decisions

  • 92% would be more likely to increase spend with faster audience fulfillment.
  • 94% would likely spend more with partners offering self-service audience-building tools.
  • Advertisers reporting the strongest ROI are five times more likely than others to receive custom audiences the same day.

Advertisers want more audience choice

  • Only 38% are extremely satisfied with the number of audiences available through their partners.
  • 95% say they would be more likely to increase spend with access to more segments.

Confidence in incrementality measurement drives investment and ROI

  • Only 40% are very confident in their partners' incrementality measurement.
  • Advertisers with high confidence in their partners' measurement spend a larger share of their digital budget on RMN/CMN and are more than twice as likely to significantly exceed ROI targets.

Campaign results often arrive too late to guide the next decision

  • Nearly half of advertisers wait at least one week for post-campaign performance data, while only 8% receive it the same day.
  • Just 32% say they can consistently use campaign results to optimize future audience targeting.

Putting audience scale and speed into practice

As audience speed and scale remain top of mind for advertisers, Gopuff — the leading instant commerce platform that delivers thousands of everyday products to customers in minutes — has shown how media networks can successfully address these priorities. Leveraging a composable commerce media solution, Gopuff can provide brand advertisers with a larger pool of audiences, activate campaigns quickly, and provide faster, more comprehensive visibility into campaign metrics.

"Advertisers increasingly expect both greater audience customization and faster activation, and we no longer have to trade one for the other," said JR Crosby, director of data partnerships at Gopuff. "After implementing a warehouse-native stack, we increased our audience segments from 100 to more than 600, and expanded audiences for our subsidiary, BevMo!, from 75 to 400. These expanded audience catalogs give our internal teams and brand partners a broader range of ready-to-use targeting options and create the groundwork for more customized segment offerings."

releases.body:
Diamond Certified utilizes research-grade methodology to stand apart from paid advertising and crowdsourced reviews.

PETALUMA, Calif., Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- American Ratings Corporation, the creator of Diamond Certified Resource, the source for consumers who love quality local companies, has published a new article on diamondcertified.org titled, "Paid Advertising vs. Earned Certifications: The Diamond Certified Difference." The piece explains how Diamond Certified differs from advertising-funded review platforms by using verified customer surveys, rigorous qualification standards, credentials checks and ongoing performance monitoring.

All organizations that certify local companies rely on one or more funding sources: advertising, donations, company-paid subscriptions or consumer-paid subscriptions. They use these funds to create methodology, conduct operations, verify information, analyze results, deny or award certifications and monitor the performance of each certified company. Some spend even more on customer satisfaction surveys and collection of original research data.

Professional ethics matter most, starting with ratings methodology.

While all certifying organizations require funding, the highly ethical ones don't allow their funding sources to bias the results. In the case of 25-year-old American Ratings Corporation, creator of Diamond Certified Resource, high ethics and accuracy start with its methodology creation, which includes funding customer satisfaction surveys and collection of original research data. Any local company can apply for the certification and pay a small rating fee, whether they pass or fail. The Diamond Certified bar is set high, though. Only companies that achieve a customer satisfaction rating of 90 or higher on a 100-point scale for Highest in Quality and Helpful Expertise and pass all required credentials checks earn Diamond Certified. Companies that fall short of these high standards don't earn Diamond Certified, regardless of how much they'd be willing to pay.

Advertising funds crowdsourced review sites.

This isn't inherently a bad thing, but it does mean these sites must generate mass traffic and monetize company owners' interest to fund their business. To gain a high volume of reviews and a large number of companies, they use review intake methods that allow non-customers to post reviews and company owners to seed and cherry-pick only satisfied customers for review solicitations. Unfortunately, they're plagued by fake and cherry-picked reviews, which has resulted in massive star score inflation. A recent study by SEO Bandwagon concludes that two-thirds of rated Google business profiles hold at least a 4.5 star rating, with plumbers and roofers scoring an average 4.9 stars. Since most local companies have a star rating score that used to be held only by the top rated, consumers are forced to wade through reviews and see if they can purge fake and misleading ones in their minds.

Diamond Certified Resource's professional ethics, ratings methodology and experienced team

Having started their customer satisfaction research in the early 1990s, the founders of Diamond Certified are pioneers in creating certifications for local companies based on customer satisfaction surveys. The Diamond Certified Research Team is also deeply experienced in ratings and research, with most managers having served on the team for more than two decades. Team members are committed to maintaining high ethical standards and producing highly accurate company ratings and research. Founder/CEO Greg Louie describes their core principle as simple but powerful. "No company is awarded Diamond Certified unless it truly earns it," he says. "Also, companies must maintain their Highest in Quality and Helpful Expertise status or we take it from them."

What is Diamond Certified?

Created by American Ratings Corporation in 2001, the Diamond Certified Research Team rates local companies (mostly contractors and service companies) on customer satisfaction, quality and Helpful Expertise®. To earn Diamond Certified, companies must apply and pay a small rating fee, pass or fail. Then the Diamond Certified Research Team puts the company through a rigorous 12-step rating process, which includes in-depth customer satisfaction surveys and credentials verification.

The rating fee does not influence the results. In fact, most companies can't qualify.

The Diamond Certified Research Team does not use any unverified online reviews. It conducts independent, research-grade ratings and research of only verified customers. Here's a simple summary of its rating process:

  • A local company applies for Diamond Certified. The Diamond Certified Research Team gathers a customer list of all past customers during the previous year or a random sample of 400 customers for larger companies. Researchers conduct telephone and email surveys of these customers at random and verify that each respondent is an actual customer before proceeding. This process prevents surveying fake or cherry-picked customers.
  • During these live telephone interviews, surveyed customers evaluate the company's work quality, whether the company provided Helpful Expertise and whether the client would use the company again. In addition to collecting customers' scores for the company, researchers record verbatim responses to open-ended questions.
  • The Diamond Certified Research Team calculates an overall customer satisfaction rating on a 100-point scale for Highest in Quality and Helpful Expertise and verifies the company's credentials. Only companies that achieve a customer satisfaction rating of 90 or higher on a 100-point scale for Highest in Quality and Helpful Expertise and pass all required credentials checks earn Diamond Certified. The team then calculates a Star Equivalent Score for each verified customer rating by weighting a Quality score on a scale of 1 to 10, a YES/NO Loyalty (intent to return) score and a YES/NO Helpful Expertise score.
  • The team produces a bound, printed report (25-30 pages) that includes verification of applicable state licenses and confirmation of required general liability and workers' compensation insurance coverage.
  • Companies that meet all of Diamond Certified's high standards are awarded the prestigious Diamond Certified, and their complete ratings and research report is posted to their Diamond Certified Company Report at www.diamondcertified.org.
  • The Diamond Certified Research Team then monitors each Diamond Certified company's performance and produces ongoing ratings and research. Each Diamond Certified Company Report is the most accurate and deeply researched report available anywhere on that company. It includes ratings, verbatim survey responses, researched articles, a capabilities table, charts, videos, photos, and expert profiles and advice.

"Companies that maintain their Diamond Certified status also agree to additional levels of oversight," says Director of Ratings David Pak. "For example, they must participate in ongoing verified customer surveys and research interviews, which are published on their Diamond Certified Company Report at diamondcertified.org."

"We also track voluntary customer feedback between survey periods," adds Greg Louie. "A company may face suspension or termination if that feedback reveals a concerning pattern of business practices, even if its overall survey score remains high."

Consumers who work with a Diamond Certified company also receive mediation support and are backed by the Diamond Certified Performance Guarantee for up to $1,000.

The Diamond Certified Difference

Diamond Certified gives consumers a researched basis for choosing a quality local company: verified customer surveys, rigorous qualification standards, credentials verification, in-depth company-specific research, and ongoing performance ratings and monitoring. Companies can't buy their way into Diamond Certified. They must earn it and keep earning it to retain it.

For consumers, that means greater confidence when choosing a high-quality local company. The ratings and research behind each Diamond Certified company are available for free at www.diamondcertified.org, so consumers can examine the ratings, read customers' verbatim responses, explore the in-depth research and make an informed choice.

American Ratings Corporation (ARC), the creator of Diamond Certified Resource, the source for consumers who love quality local companies, rates local companies by surveying only their verified real customers to produce the country's most accurate ratings of local companies. It also creates deeply researched company reports and consumer guides that give consumers the best companies plus the best advice for choosing a local Auto, Home, Health or Personal service type of company.

releases.title: Hasan Minhaj Named Recipient of the AAF's 2026 Cultural Force Award
releases.body:
Comedian, Writer, Actor, & Producer 186K Films Honored for Shaping Culture at the Intersection of Comedy, Media, and Marketing

WASHINGTON, Sept. 25, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The American Advertising Federation (AAF), "The Unifying Voice for Advertising", today announced that comedian, writer, and producer Hasan Minhaj will receive the 2026 Cultural Force Award, a special honor presented as part of the AAF's long standing Advertising Hall of Achievement (AHOA). While the AHOA recognizes advertising professionals age 40 and under, the Cultural Force Award — introduced in 2023 — honors a public figure outside the industry whose work has nonetheless shaped how brands advertise, market, and reach new audiences.

Minhaj joins the AHOA Class of 2026, alongside eight previously announced honorees who have found ways to make their impact on advertising. Previous Cultural Force Award recipients include former NBA All-Star Chris Paul in 2023; writer, producer, and actress Issa Rae in 2024; and supermodel Ashley Graham in 2025.

Today's announcement comes as Minhaj's Netflix feature film Best of the Best — produced by his company 186K Films and co-written by and starring Minhaj — premiered globally on September 18, 2026.

While Minhaj is known for his career as a stand-up comedian, writer, producer, political commentator, and actor, he has also become one of the advertising industry's most recognizable creative collaborators. Notably, Minhaj is the face of Adobe's multi-year Acrobat campaign, including starring as a marketing executive in Adobe's original branded comedy series The Marketers — playing, in effect, the very industry now honoring him.

"The Cultural Force Award is reserved for individuals who have not only shaped culture, but challenged it, pushing conversations forward, redefining narratives, and leaving audiences thinking a little deeper. Hasan's work has consistently done exactly that," said Steve Pacheco, President & CEO of the AAF. "Whether unpacking complex social issues, questioning systems of power, or simply reminding us that the right storytelling has the power to cut through noise -- he's created a voice that resonates far beyond entertainment."

"I've played a marketing exec in Adobe ads for three years, so getting an actual advertising award feels like incredible method acting finally paying off," said Minhaj. "In all seriousness, it's an honor — advertising forced me to say 'synergy' out loud on camera, so really, this serves as a two-way apology."

Minhaj will be presented the award on Thursday, November 19, at Pier Sixty in New York City, alongside this year's AAF's Advertising Hall of Achievement inductees. Corporate sponsors for this year's event include LinkedIn, Dentsu, Disney Advertising, Google, TikTok, AMC Networks, Amazon Ads, Paramount Advertising, TelevisaUnivision, Omnicom Media, 3C Ventures, Albertson's Media Collective, Known, and WPP Media.

For further details about the AAF AHOA dinner and ceremonies, including sponsorship opportunities, visit aaf.org/ahoa. At The Moment Media (ATM) is the official media partner of the 2026 Advertising Hall of Achievement Ceremonies.

About Hasan Minhaj

Hasan Minhaj is a two-time Peabody Award-winning comedian best known for his breakout Netflix special Homecoming King and his political satire series Patriot Act with Hasan Minhaj, winner of a Peabody, an Emmy, and a Television Academy Honor. He is the co-founder and CEO of 186K Films, whose feature Best of the Best — directed by Lena Khan and starring Maitreyi Ramakrishnan and Priyanka Kedia — premieres globally on Netflix September 18, 2026. Minhaj co-wrote the film with Prashanth Venkataramanujam and stars in it. He hosts the podcast and digital series Hasan Minhaj Doesn't Know and was a senior correspondent on Comedy Central's The Daily Show with Jon Stewart.

ABOUT AAF (AMERICAN ADVERTISING FEDERATION)

The American Advertising Federation (AAF), established in 1905, is the nation's oldest national advertising trade association and serves as "The Unifying Voice for Advertising." Guided by its Board of Directors, the AAF leads the industry's premier programs and events, including the Advertising Hall of Fame, Advertising Hall of Achievement, American Advertising Awards, ADMERICA, Advertising Day on the Hill, the Most Promising Students Program, and HBCUs for Advertising. Together, these initiatives support a nationwide network of more than 125 professional chapters, 140 collegiate chapters, and more than 65 corporate members representing leading media and technology companies, advertisers, and agencies. Learn more at https://aaf.org. 

ABOUT AAF ADVERTISING HALL OF ACHIEVEMENT (AHOA)

For more than 30 years, the AAF Advertising Hall of Achievement has recognized exceptional advertising leaders age 40 and younger who are shaping the future of the industry. Inductees are selected through a rigorous, two-round judging process led by Hall of Achievement alumni and senior industry executives. Established by the American Advertising Federation (AAF) in 1993, the program is one of the industry's highest honors for emerging leaders.
